key_insight: How patient EHR sequences are grouped during pretraining can meaningfully change foundation model performance, even without changing the model itself.
clinical_relevance: Better sequence composition during EHR model pretraining may improve downstream clinical prediction tasks and support more reliable decision-support tools.
method: Compared a global-stream pretraining baseline with alternative ways of composing patient trajectories into training windows.
Evaluated the methods on four MIMIC-IV v2.2 clinical prediction tasks.
Tested whether gains carried over to four additional settings, including INSPIRE and eICU-CRD.
evidence_signal: Across four MIMIC-IV v2.2 tasks, the best method improved macro AUROC, AUPRC, F1, and balanced accuracy, with gains also generalizing to four extra evaluation settings.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective benchmarks, so real-world benefit and robustness will still need external validation and careful implementation.
paper_title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining
